question: Should OpenClaw core accept model-controlled continuation, delegation, volitional compaction, and opt-in trusted cross-session return delivery as a core runtime feature in this PR?
rationale: The PR creates new model-facing tools, config/defaults, persistent state, Codex protocol integration, session targeting, and trusted internal delivery behavior that automated review cannot safely approve as product/security policy.

options.title: Accept after exact-head proof
options.body: Keep the feature in core, but require clean exact-head or merge-head proof plus explicit approval for config, state, Codex, and trusted-return semantics before landing.

options.title: Narrow the first landing
options.body: Land only self-session continuation and compaction first, and defer cross-session targeting or trusted fanout to a smaller security-reviewed follow-up.

options.title: Pause for async-runtime design
options.body: Hold this PR and fold the useful implementation into a broader maintainer-owned async action and continuation design.

recommendation.title: Accept after exact-head proof
recommendation.body: Keep the feature in core, but require clean exact-head or merge-head proof plus explicit approval for config, state, Codex, and trusted-return semantics before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current-main routing signal across agent tools, system-event authority, task-flow persistence, and Codex dynamic-tool surfaces.
